rendered: The document does not describe the Cyrene-based separation as run at room temperature. The separation is run hot: the cathode scraps are stirred in Cyrene at After stirring at 100 °C for[1] and the black mass is separated while the mixture is still hot. The reason given is that the PVDF binder is barely soluble in Cyrene[2] at low temperature, and it dissolves quickly at a higher temperature. The authors state that PVDF would precipitate out if the temperature was low.[3] Hot centrifugation and hot filtration are therefore used to separate the black mass from Cyrene and to prevent the reprecipitation of PVDF. Room temperature enters only later, in the recovery of PVDF. The hot supernatant is cooled down to room[4] temperature to induce phase separation[5], so that PVDF and carbon black precipitate and the PVDF/CB composite and the recycled Cyrene can be recovered. Room-temperature filtration also appears only as a comparison in the FTIR analysis, where the cathode powder filtered at room temperature still shows the PVDF band, indicating that PVDF reprecipitated on cooling, while the hot-filtered powder does not.
